So to Captain Cocke’s, and there sat and talked, especially with his Counsellor, about his [prize goods](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9633/), that hath done him good turne, being of the company with [Captain Fisher](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9067/), his name [Godderson](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9553/); here I supped and so [home](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8994/) to bed, with great content that the plague is decreased to 152, the whole being but 330."], [258, "It is true we have gone through great melancholy because of the great [plague](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/301/), and I put to great charges by it, by keeping my family long at [Woolwich](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1675/), and myself and another part of my family, my clerks, at my charge at [Greenwich](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/2673/), and a mayde at London; but I hope [the King](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/344/) will give us some satisfaction for that. But now the plague is abated almost to nothing, and I intending to get to London as fast as I can. My family, that is [my wife](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/150/) and maids, having been there these two or three weeks. The Dutch war goes on very ill, by reason of lack of money; having none to hope for, all being put into disorder by [a new Act](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/14126/) that is made as an experiment to bring credit to the [Exchequer](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/290/), for goods and money to be advanced upon the credit of that Act. I have never lived so merrily (besides that I never got so much) as I have done this plague time, by my [Lord Bruncker’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/4135/) and [Captain Cocke’s](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/3164/) good company, and the acquaintance of [Mrs. Knipp](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9483/), [Coleman](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9387/) and [her husband](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9386/), and [Mr. Laneare](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9388/), and great store of dancings we have had at my cost (which I was willing to indulge myself and wife) at [my lodgings](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/8994/). The great evil of this year, and the only one indeed, is the fall of my [Lord of Sandwich](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/112/), whose mistake about the [prizes](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/9633/) hath undone him, I believe, as to interest at Court; though sent (for a little palliating it) Embassador into Spayne, which he is now fitting himself for. But the Duke of Albemarle goes with [the Prince](http://www.pepysdiary.com/encyclopedia/1357/) to sea this next year, and my Lord very meanly spoken of; and, indeed, his miscarriage about the prize goods is not to be excused, to suffer a company of rogues to go away with ten times as much as himself, and the blame of all to be deservedly laid upon him.[1](https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1665/12/#fn1-1665-12-31)"]], "next_offset": null}
